title: Wrong Number, Right Person
use_cases: Use when promoting a contemporary romance novel focused on economic disparity
Implement when categorizing stories involving mistaken identity or wrong number tropes
Configure when highlighting billionaire romance narratives with strong female leads
content:
Maya Hendricks is twenty eight years old, raising her son Eli alone in Chicago, and running out of road. She works three jobs, counts every dollar, and has not asked anyone for help in fourteen months. She is not proud of very much right now. But she is proud of that. One cold November night she does something embarrassing. She texts the wrong number. A message meant for her sister goes to a complete stranger instead. That stranger replies. I think you have the wrong number. But I am listening, if you want. His name is Nate. She does not know his last name. She does not know that he is Nathaniel Cole. founder of NovaCorp, worth eleven billion dollars, and completely alone in a life that looks perfect from the outside. He does not tell her. She does not ask. What begins as a mistake becomes something neither of them can explain or walk away from. Two people from completely different worlds finding the one thing money cannot buy and survival cannot teach. But secrets do not stay buried. And love built on half truths must eventually face the whole story. Wrong Number, Right Person…. because some mistakes change everything.
